The failing test `testMultipleChildOptions` uses the parser to parse an array containing the options "--child" with argument "test" and "--sub" with argument "anotherTest". The test is failing due to an issue where minimum and maximum constraints on a Group do not account for other Groups properly.

The current bug report indicates the root cause: When a Group is a child of another Group and minimum or maximum constraints are set on the parent Group, the parent's constraints are not affected by the presence or absence of the child Group. This happens because Groups themselves are never added to the CommandLine instance. Therefore, the `hasOption(Group)` call on CommandLine returns false, and the Group is not counted. As a result, the parent's minimum or maximum constraints do not reflect the state correctly.

The key insight from the bug report is that the `WriteableCommandLine#addOption(Option)` method should be used in a way that the presence of any child option of a Group should indicate the Group's presence, effectively adding the Group option if any child is present.

Looking at the code of `WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption(Option)`, we see that:
- The option is added to an internal collection (`options.add(option)`),
- The preferred name and triggers of the option are registered in a map,
- But there is a comment "// ensure that all parent options are also added" and no code actually implementing this.

Thus, the current implementation adds only the given option but does not propagate this addition to parent Groups.

Also, from `WriteableCommandLineImpl.hasOption(Option)`, the method simply checks whether the option is present in the collection without any special logic for Groups. Therefore, if a Group option itself was never added (only its children were), `hasOption(group)` returns false.

This matches precisely the scenario described in the bug report: the presence of a child option in a Group does not trigger adding the Group itself into the CommandLine. Consequently, the constraints on the Group calling `hasOption` to check its children do not see the Group considered present, breaking minimum and maximum checks.

No recent bug reports seem directly relevant other than the current one.

# Diagnosis

The bug occurs because `WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption(Option)` does not propagate the addition of an option upwards to its parent Groups. Therefore, even when child options of a Group are added to the command line, the Group itself is never added. Later checks on the CommandLine that ask whether a Group option is present return false because the Group option was never added, breaking checking of minimum and maximum constraints on that Group and causing the test failure in `testMultipleChildOptions`.

# Suggested fix location (based on this diagnosis)

The fix should be applied in the implementation of `WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption(Option)` to recursively add parent Groups of an option when the option itself is added, ensuring Groups appear in the CommandLine when any child option is present.

Furthermore, it may be useful to check `WriteableCommandLineImpl.hasOption(Option)` to ensure it works correctly once the Group options are propagated in addOption.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
